overview: 53 official Group 1 Qs (2008–2024) on RBI tools, banking reforms, GST, Finance Commissions, taxes, markets and budget. Up to 2019 mostly one-liners (who, when, which number); 2023–24 shifted hard to statement-based items (often 4–5 statements on current schemes) plus A-R and match lists. Heaviest: Finance Commissions (9), RBI/monetary policy (8), banking reforms (8), GST (7).

possibility.what_they_ask: which committee recommended an institution, which body launched a product (RuPay – NPCI), coverage figures

possibility.angle: RBI and monetary policy – CRR, SLR, credit control, inflation
possibility.what_they_ask: effect of a CRR change, what counts for SLR, quantitative vs qualitative tools, MCLR/MSF mechanics, inflation measure and current food/headline/core order

possibility.angle: Banking and financial sector reforms, digital payments
possibility.what_they_ask: nationalisation date and number, Narasimham committee name, Basel III ratios, Jan Dhan, EASE reforms, RBI-DPI base and parameters, e-RUPI / UPI features
NPA 90-day definition, what para-banking includes, bank slogans

possibility.angle: Financial markets – money and gilt markets
possibility.what_they_ask: T-bill tenors, what the gilt-edged market covers
which exchange has the bulk of trade (NSE), recent SEBI frameworks (25% debt for large corporates, bond ticket size), RBI vs SEBI schemes

possibility.angle: Indian tax system and recent changes
possibility.what_they_ask: largest tax source (time-bound), VAT features, problem of multiple rates, A-R on tax simplicity
items outside GST (petroleum), anti-profiteering, how rates change, 122nd Bill, destination basis, GST Council under Art. 279A
Art. 268–271 levy/collection/sharing pattern, repealed articles, CSS 'core of the core' tier
chairmen by number, award period, base year, criterion with highest weight, vertical vs horizontal factors, effect of grants→devolution shift
which indicator signals bad fiscal health (rising debt-GDP); natural targets: FRBM targets, types of deficit
effect of deficit financing, current budget proposals (Interim Budget 2024 green-energy items)

traps.trap: Reverses the direction of a monetary tool's effect
traps.spot: 'increasing CRR will increase credit', 'rise in lending capacity'
traps.fix: CRR/SLR up = less lendable money, less credit, less demand; down = the opposite
traps.pyq: 'CRR [...] increases' → I and II only [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#72]; 'increasing CRR increases credit creation' false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#77]

traps.trap: Puts a quantitative tool in the qualitative list (or a credit target in SLR)
traps.spot: Negative 'does not include' or 'SLR in the form of' lists
traps.fix: Quantitative: bank rate, repo, OMO, CRR, SLR; qualitative: margins, moral suasion, rationing; SLR assets = cash, gold, unencumbered G-secs
traps.pyq: → Bank rate policy [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#26]; priority-sector loans not SLR [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#73]

traps.trap: Alters one rung of a numeric ladder
traps.spot: Basel ratios, DPI parameters, number of priorities
traps.fix: RBI Basel III: CET1 5.5, Tier 1 7, total 9, +CCB 2.5 = 11.5; RBI-DPI has 5 parameters, base March 2018

traps.trap: Makes a constitutional body 'statutory first' or swaps its dispute forum
traps.spot: GST Council statements with history or adjudication claims
traps.fix: GST Council created directly by Art. 279A (101st Amendment, 2016); defects in appointment do not invalidate proceedings; disputes go to a mechanism the Council sets up
Art. 271 surcharges and cesses go wholly to the Union; Art. 270 taxes are shared

traps.trap: Widens scope to a body not covered
traps.spot: 'for both PSBs and NBFCs', 'transparency to direct tax laws'
traps.fix: EASE reforms = PSBs only; GST is an indirect-tax reform
traps.pyq: EASE IV false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#74]; GST I false → II and III [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#48]

traps.trap: Gives a scheme to the wrong agency
traps.spot: 'built by a startup consortium', 'SEBI along with RBI introduced'
traps.fix: Hello! UPI, RuPay, e-RUPI = NPCI; Retail Direct = RBI alone
traps.pyq: Hello! UPI statement false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#62]; Retail Direct false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#70]; RuPay → NPCI [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#79]

traps.trap: Swaps the sector a budget measure belongs to
traps.spot: Budget-proposal lists with one item moved from another sector, or 'optional' for 'mandatory'
traps.fix: Interim Budget 2024: VGF for offshore wind, not solar; CBG blending to be mandatory in phases

techniques.name: Money-flow arrow test
techniques.how: Draw the arrow: tool up → bank reserves locked → credit ↓ → money supply ↓ → demand ↓. Every statement must match the arrow's direction.
techniques.example: CRR hike: fall in money circulation and low demand fit; rise in purchasing power and lending capacity run against [...] → 'I and II only' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#72]

techniques.name: FC sequence ladder
techniques.how: Memorise FC number → chair → period as one ladder (10 Pant, 11 Khusro, 12 Rangarajan, 13 Kelkar, 14 Reddy 2015-20, 15 N.K. Singh, 16 Panagariya). Use it for match lists, award periods and base years.
techniques.example: 10-Pant (II) and 13-Kelkar (III) leave only 'II IV I III' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#79]; 14th FC period 1 Apr 2015–31 Mar 2020 [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#53]

techniques.name: Fiscal-health sign check
techniques.how: Good fiscal administration lowers debt, deficits and interest burden and raises tax-GDP. In a 'hampers' question pick the option moving the wrong way.
techniques.example: Only 'increasing the debt GDP ratio' worsens health → option 1 [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#24]

techniques.name: Feature-of-design elimination for taxes
techniques.how: Recall what the tax was designed to do (input credit, no cascading, invoice trail, wider base). The option contradicting that design is the 'not a feature'.
techniques.example: Non-cascading, harmonised, self-enforcing all fit VAT; 'diminish revenue buoyancy' contradicts → option 1 [group1-prelims-2010#85]

techniques.name: Tied vs untied transfer logic
techniques.how: Tax devolution = untied; grants (esp. CSS) = tied. A shift from grants to devolution raises untied money in State hands.
techniques.example: Shift to devolution → 'increase in share of unconditional transfers' [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#21]

techniques.name: Date-stamp the current-affairs statement
techniques.how: For 'present trends', 'recent' budget or index items, fix the month/year the paper was set and check each claim against that period only.
techniques.example: Early 2024: retail inflation was easing, so 'considerably increased' falls; Bharat Atta and Bharat Dal hold → II and IV [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#73]

confusions.b: SLR (cash, gold, G-secs with the bank)
confusions.remember: CRR earns nothing and sits with RBI; SLR is held by the bank itself
ICRR is an extra reserve on incremental deposits (NDTL), not on lending
MSF = repo + 25 bp, overnight, emergency; equal to Bank Rate
Volume of credit (rates, reserves, OMO) vs direction of credit (margins, moral suasion)
Committee on the Financial System vs Committee on Banking Sector Reforms
Centre vs States share (42% under 14th FC) vs share among States (criteria weights)
Income distance 50% vs 45%; 15th adds demographic performance and tax effort
Surcharge is Union-only, not in the divisible pool
GST rates and exemptions vs devolution of divisible pool
RuPay, UPI, e-RUPI, Hello! UPI vs Retail Direct, DPI
BSE oldest and most listings; NSE largest turnover
RBI is stricter; with CCB total 11.5%
'Para' = ancillary services (cards, insurance, factoring), not a borrower group

anchors: 1991 Narasimham Committee = Committee on the Financial System
NPA = interest/principal overdue more than 90 days
RBI Basel III: CET1 5.5%, Tier 1 7%, CRAR 9%, + CCB 2.5% = 11.5%
MSF = repo + 0.25% = Bank Rate; MCLR includes tenor premium
CPI-Combined is RBI's inflation anchor since 2014–16; WPI was the headline measure in 2008
Five petroleum products outside GST until the Council recommends: crude, petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas
14th FC: 2015–20, 42% share, base year 2014–15, income distance 50%
FC chairs: 10 K.C. Pant, 11 A.M. Khusro, 12 C. Rangarajan, 13 Vijay Kelkar, 14 Y.V. Reddy, 15 N.K. Singh
RBI-DPI: base March 2018, 5 parameters, published since 2021
Deficit financing by printing money → inflationary
checklist: Draw the money-flow arrow: does each statement move in the same direction?
Which agency owns the product or scheme – RBI, SEBI, NPCI, DFS, Council?
For a number (ratio, parameter count, days, percent) recall the full ladder before judging one rung
Is the body constitutional, statutory or executive – and since when?
Check scope words: PSBs only? indirect taxes only? greenfield only?
For 'current' figures or orderings, fix the year the paper was set
For FC items: which commission number, vertical or horizontal, which criterion?
